shape_definitions.resource-heavy: time_network(size, "fan", seed=20261116) (fan: one root -> size-2 concurrent activities -> one join)
shape_definitions.constraint-heavy: time_network(size, "dag", seed=20261116) plus TimeActivityConstraint(START_NO_EARLIER_THAN) on every 7th activity

definitions.constraint_target_formula: TIME_PROJECT_START + timedelta(days=(index % 21) + 1) for index in range(0, size, 7)
definitions.timeout_policy: each cell runs in its own subprocess; every mode is bounded by signal.setitimer(ITIMER_REAL) inside the child and a hard subprocess timeout in the parent; a cell with no phase budget left is recorded SKIPPED_BUDGET
notes: Measurement only: this harness adds scripts/p0n2_runtime_matrix.py and the four evidence files under docs/workspace/evidence/p0n-runtime-activation-2026-11-20/ and changes no product code, test, or configuration.

The worker process-mode path ran against the fixed executor: commit 5b4cfb7104cbd4952d60af9734cfe1b559aa923f ("fix(p0n): drain the child result pipe before join in process placement") is the recorded run HEAD, so every worker number here includes the pipe-drain fix. The defect it removes: the parent joined the child before reading the result pipe, so a pickled SchedulingJobResult above the ~64 KiB pipe buffer deadlocked and the job was retried as SCHEDULING_JOB_TIMEOUT (regression test: tests/scheduling/test_scheduling_job_executor_process.py::test_result_larger_than_the_pipe_buffer_does_not_deadlock).

constraint-heavy cells pass the fixture's own (unconstrained) project_finish to time_schedule, exactly like scripts/p0n_multi_project_benchmark.py::run_project. Because the START_NO_EARLIER_THAN list pushes work later than that finish, the recorded total float for those cells is negative; min_total_float_hours/max_total_float_hours are stored per run so the effect is visible instead of hidden.

This host runs other work items in parallel; the same PostgreSQL instance is shared. Each worker run seeds its own unique tenant scope, so rows never overlap, but wall-clock numbers can include contention noise.

note_corrections.was: The worker process-mode path runs against src/construction_pm/scheduling_job_executor.py as it stands in this working tree, which carries an uncommitted fix from another work item: the parent now drains the result pipe (non-blocking poll/recv) before joining the child. Before that fix, two exploratory 5000-activity process-mode runs started by this harness deadlocked with the job child blocked in pipe_write once the pickled SchedulingJobResult exceeded the ~64 KB pipe buffer; those runs were terminated, are not part of this evidence, and their job rows were left as found (expired LEASED, cancelled by the fixing work item).
note_corrections.now: The worker process-mode path ran against the fixed executor: commit 5b4cfb7104cbd4952d60af9734cfe1b559aa923f ("fix(p0n): drain the child result pipe before join in process placement") is the recorded run HEAD, so every worker number here includes the pipe-drain fix. The defect it removes: the parent joined the child before reading the result pipe, so a pickled SchedulingJobResult above the ~64 KiB pipe buffer deadlocked and the job was retried as SCHEDULING_JOB_TIMEOUT (regression test: tests/scheduling/test_scheduling_job_executor_process.py::test_result_larger_than_the_pipe_buffer_does_not_deadlock).

post_phase_rerun_note: Two 100k cells exceeded the orchestrated phase deadline (960 s) and were measured in separate subprocess invocations with an explicit --mode-budget: 100000/resource-heavy (1500 s) and 100000/constraint-heavy (1800 s per mode). They replace the SKIPPED_BUDGET records; the superseded status, its exact error text and the overriding command are kept in each cell (post_phase_rerun, superseded_record, mode_budget_override_s).
